summary.headline: India Shelter Q1FY26: AUM up 34% YoY to Rs 8,712 crore and PAT up 43% to Rs 119 crore, but 30+ DPD rose about 100 bps to ~4.5%.
summary.overview: Q1FY26 (quarter ended June 30, 2025) showed strong growth: AUM Rs 8,712 crore (+34% YoY, +6% QoQ), disbursements Rs 887 crore (+24% YoY), and PAT Rs 119 crore (+43% YoY, +10% QoQ) with ROE of 17.2%. Asset quality weakened seasonally and from macro stress: 30+ DPD rose about 100 bps YoY, Stage 3 reached 1.2% (+10 bps YoY), and credit cost was 0.5%. Management guided that July 30+ DPD was flat versus Q1, and it maintained its FY26 guidance on branches, spreads, credit cost and loan growth.

financial_highlights.change: ROE crossed 17% for first time post listing; ROA +20 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: Bucket cost of funds / marginal cost of funds
financial_highlights.change: Bucket CoF -10 bps QoQ; marginal CoF -30 bps YoY
Stable YoY despite leverage rising from 2.6x to 2.9x
vs regulatory threshold of Rs 40 crore

financial_highlights.value: Rs 650 crore+ plus undrawn sanctions of Rs 560 crore

segments.name: Home loans (HL)
segments.commentary: Stage 3 reported as same as LAP (about 1.2%); 30+ DPD estimated at 30-40 bps below the 4.5% overall level. Average tenor about 7 years behavioural, 15 years contractual.

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP)
segments.commentary: 30+ DPD about 30 bps above the 4.5% overall level; LTVs around 45-47%, with LAP restricted to self-occupied residential property. LAP is about 43% of AUM (57:43 HL:LAP mix), against a target of 60:40.

segments.name: Direct assignment (DA)
segments.commentary: Used only for LAP; DA income about 1.8% of average total assets versus 1.7% a year earlier. DA stays at 15-17% of AUM, with DA growth of about 30-35% YoY expected.

guidance_outlook: Branch additions of about 40-45 for FY26; 24 branches added in Q1, taking the total to 290+ branches.
Spreads to stay above 6% in the medium term; spread to improve by about 20 bps further in FY26.
Credit cost of about 40-50 bps maintained for the year.
Loan growth of about 30-35% maintained; AUM growth of 30-35% projected for the period.
Bucket cost of funds expected to fall another 20 bps by year-end; sizeable benefit expected by Q3 as MCLR-linked borrowings reset.
Opex to AUM to fall 15-20 bps per year; NIM expected to stay about 9% as leverage rises.
Leverage to reach about 4x by FY28, with ROA about 4.5% and ROE about 18% in the medium term. Capital raise expected after FY28 closure.
Pass-through of rate cuts to customers deferred to Q3; management indicated a possible 5-10 bps pass-on.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 290+ as of June 30, 2025, with 24 added in Q1 and 40-45 planned for FY26.

Around 1,700 loan officers across the branches; productivity measured as files disbursed per loan officer, which was just under 2 in Q1 (seasonally lean), with a target of at least 10% annual improvement.
Gujarat growth deliberately slowed to hold the 6% spread; Uttarakhand branch expansion limited due to hilly terrain; Karnataka expansion paused.
Leverage at 2.9x against a capital adequacy ratio of about 57-58%; next equity raise planned after FY28 closure, when leverage reaches about 4.5x.
demand_pricing: Competition: management said it sees no undercutting in its Tier 2/Tier 3 niche; the main competitive pressure is from poaching of employees.
Borrowing mix: about 90% variable-rate (about 35% repo-linked, rest MCLR-linked) and about 10% fixed. Loan book: about 15% variable, about 30% semi-variable (fixed for 3 years), and about 55% fixed.
Incremental disbursements: about 50-60% are semi-variable; aspiration for 65% of assets to be variable or semi-variable within two years.
Incremental yield is about 15.0%, the same as the book yield.
Borrower profile: FOIR of 50-55%; monthly income of Rs 30,000-65,000; behavioural tenor of about 6 years for LAP and 7 years for HL.
PMAY CLSS 2: about 1,500 applications in process, 500-700 pending, and more than 200 customers have received the first subsidy tranche.
Attrition: regrettable sales attrition around 20-23%; ESOP coverage to rise from about 350 to about 800 employees (about 25% of staff, aiming for over 50%).
Repayment rate supported by balance transfer-out held at 5-6%, at the low end of its 12-18 month range.

qa_highlights.question: Is 30+ DPD trend in Q2 and credit cost guidance at risk, given 30+ DPD near 4.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: July 30+ DPD was about flat with Q1 (maybe 2 bps lower). Management kept credit cost at 40-50 bps for the year and said Q2 should be stable with Q3 targeted better than Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Cost of funds and pass-through outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About 90% of borrowings are variable; bucket CoF fell 20 bps in the last four months and another 20 bps is expected by year-end. Pass-through is deferred to Q3; because only 15% of assets are variable, a 25 bps cut would have little portfolio yield impact.

qa_highlights.question: Which states are under stress?
qa_highlights.answer: MP is the outlier and is improving slowly with new leadership; Karnataka is stabilising after the Jan-Feb 2025 issue, and expansion there is paused. UP has one of the lowest delinquency rates, and Tamil Nadu shows a slight uptick in line with the national trend.

qa_highlights.question: How are ECL and PCR assumptions reflecting macro stress?
qa_highlights.answer: PD has risen slightly with macro factors, but LGD is about 11% historically (from about 2,500 resolutions), offset by low LTVs. Management said the overlay built in adequate buffers; ECL is Rs 67 crore against a Rs 40 crore regulatory threshold.

qa_highlights.question: Is the LAP mix a risk, and should growth shift back to HL?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP's Stage 3 matches HL, but its 30+ DPD runs about 30 bps higher. Management is targeting a 60:40 HL:LAP mix, currently 57:43, and it is not planning to slow LAP sharply.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable steady-state 30+ DPD and Stage 2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that 4-4.5% 30+ DPD is directionally practical as a steady state but said the target is to push it lower. It expects 30+ DPD to settle around 3.2-3.3% by FY26 year-end.

risks_watch: 30+ DPD at about 4.5% (up about 100 bps YoY), with MP still elevated and Karnataka stabilising; watch whether Q2 holds at Q1 levels, as management guided.
Stage 2 rose this quarter; management did not give a Q2 Stage 3 number, only that it would be below Q1 (1.2%).
Macro stress in MFI and unsecured segments; management acknowledged some underwriting pressure across the industry.
Sales attrition of about 20-23% (regrettable); ESOP rollout intended to address retention.
Rate pass-through timing and the MCLR reset benefit depend on Q3 timing; the spread guidance of 20 bps depends on that reset.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, margins and the medium-term ROE path, but cautious and somewhat hedged on near-term asset quality: management repeatedly said Q2 should be stable with Q1, gave no firm Stage 3 number for Q2, and tied recovery to Q3.
key_quotes: We delivered AUM growth of 34% year -on-year, reaching an AUM of Rs. 8,712 crores.
So, we feel this quarter should largely remain stable.
So, we are giving the same guidance of 40 to 50 bps of credit cost for the year.

adds.what: Branches: 40-45 planned for FY26 (24 added in Q1, total 290+)

growth.why: Management guides loan/AUM growth of 30-35% for FY26, backed by 40-45 branch additions (24 done in Q1) and a 20 bps cost-of-funds cut, with the brief reporting AUM +34% YoY and PAT +43% in the quarter.
